book.title: A Good Man Is Hard to Find
book.author: Flannery O'Connor

beats.narration: You have this little boy named Harry who tells people his name is Bevel. Well, this story breaks my heart. He's 5 years old, completely neglected by his hungover, perpetually partying parents. His babysitter,

storyboard.claim: Harry, who calls himself Bevel, is five and completely neglected by his hungover, partying parents.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty apartment room with a house icon and nobody in it.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the empty home shows absence; the boy's age and name are carried by the audio.

beats.narration: Mrs. Connin, takes him out to a rural river healing. There is a preacher standing waist deep in the slow red river, singing and preaching to a crowd. Mhm. He takes this little boy, swings him

storyboard.claim: Mrs. Connin takes him to a river healing where a preacher stands waist deep, preaching to a crowd.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A riverbank with the water icon, empty of people.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the neglected home to the river.
storyboard.addedInformation: The scene shifts from indoors to the river where the story turns.

beats.narration: upside down, and violently plunges his head into the water, telling him he now counts.

storyboard.claim: The preacher plunges the boy's head into the water and tells him he now counts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same riverbank and water icon, kept.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same river; the callout names the preacher's promise.
storyboard.addedInformation: The promise that he counts is what draws him back later.

beats.narration: Later, to escape the miserable, silent neglect of his parents' apartment, where he's just wandering around, emptying ashtrays on the rug and watching them sleep off hangovers,

storyboard.claim: To escape the silent neglect of the apartment, where he empties ashtrays and watches his parents sleep,
storyboard.concreteVisual: The empty apartment room with the house icon again.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back from the river to the home of beat 0.
storyboard.addedInformation: Restates why he leaves: nothing at home holds him.

beats.narration: the boy returns to the river He wads in, trying to baptize himself looking for the kingdom of Christ the preacher promised him.

storyboard.claim: The boy returns to the river and wades in, trying to baptize himself to find the kingdom of Christ.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The riverbank with the water icon, empty.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the river of beats 1-2.
storyboard.addedInformation: He seeks the promise alone, without the preacher.

beats.narration: He fights the water. He's choking, but eventually the current catches him like a long gentle hand and pulls him swiftly forward and down to his drowning death.

storyboard.claim: He fights the water, but the current catches him like a long gentle hand and pulls him down to his death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same riverbank and water icon, kept, still empty.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same river; now the current takes him.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the empty river implies he is gone; the death is carried by audio and callout.

beats.narration: It is horrifying on a literal physical A neglected child drowns, but spiritually, textually, the river current catching him like a gentle hand is the arrival of grace.

storyboard.claim: Literally a neglected child drowns, but spiritually the current catching him is the arrival of grace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter with two buckets: the literal drowning and the spiritual grace.
storyboard.onScreenText: Literally: a child drowns / Spiritually: grace arrives
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Steps back from the story to the two ways of reading it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the double reading the analysis rests on.

beats.narration: Grace is a terrifying physical force that often ends in death in these stories. Wait, I have to stop here and really interrogate this. How on earth is getting shot in the chest three times by a serial killer or a

storyboard.claim: Grace is a terrifying physical force that often ends in death, like being shot by a serial killer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Misfit standing in the woods with an angry, threatening face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the drowning to the other death the hosts name: the Misfit's killing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the killer the host mentions on screen as the face of violent grace.

beats.narration: neglected 5-year-old drowning alone in a muddy river grace to a modern listener? To me, that's just a bleak, horrifying, utterly hopeless tragedy. It feels like total nihilism masked

storyboard.claim: To a modern listener a child drowning alone is a bleak, horrifying, hopeless tragedy, nihilism masked as religion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon in the woods, nobody present.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host objects to calling these deaths grace.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grave states the plain reading: death, nothing more.

beats.narration: as religion. It absolutely feels hopeless if you were looking at it through our modern secular materialist lens. Right. Because we value life.

storyboard.claim: It feels hopeless only if you look at it through our modern secular materialist lens, because we value life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow: Modern secular lens -> Feels hopeless.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains where the objection of beat 8 comes from.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the hopelessness to the lens, not to the story.

beats.narration: Exactly. Today, we generally believe that the ultimate good is a long, comfortable, painless physical life.

storyboard.claim: Today we believe the ultimate good is a long, comfortable, painless physical life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text card on an abstract background.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the value behind the modern lens.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried; states the value the lens measures by.

beats.narration: But to understand this trap, you have to completely immerse yourself in O'Connor's fiercely strictly orthodox Catholic Okay. So, how does she see it?

storyboard.claim: To understand the story you have to immerse yourself in O'Connor's strictly orthodox Catholic view.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter with two buckets: the modern secular lens and O'Connor's Catholic lens.
storyboard.onScreenText: Modern secular lens / O'Connor's Catholic lens
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the modern view to O'Connor's.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the two lenses the next passage compares.
